items.label: Lazy Consensus
items.description: A decision is assumed approved unless objections are raised within a specified timeframe.

items.label: Do-ocracy
items.description: Decisions are made by those who take initiative and carry out the work.

items.label: Consensus Decision-Making
items.description: All members must agree. Best for important decisions in small groups. Does not work well for low stakes decsions.

items.label: Rotational Leadership
items.description: Decision-making responsibilities rotate among members.

items.label: Modified Consensus
items.description: Attempts to reach full agreement first, but falls back to voting if consensus isn’t possible.

items.label: Consensus Seeking with Delegates
items.description: Members provide input, and delegates refine decisions to seek broad agreement.

items.label: Sociocracy
items.description: Decisions are made in small, interconnected circles with feedback loops connecting the organization.

items.label: Supermajority Rule
items.description: A higher threshold (e.g., 2/3 or 3/4) must be met for a decision to pass. Can be a great fallback for when consensus fails.

items.label: Ranked Choice Voting
items.description: Members rank options by preference, and votes are redistributed until one option has a majority.

items.label: Range Voting
items.description: Members score each option, and the option with the highest total or average score wins.

items.label: Majority Rule
items.description: A decision is approved if it receives more than 50% of the votes.

items.label: Approval Voting
items.description: Members vote for all options they find acceptable; the option with the most approvals wins.

items.label: Weighted Voting
items.description: Votes carry different weights based on criteria like financial contribution or seniority.

items.label: Cumulative Voting
items.description: Members distribute a set number of votes across one or more options, often to express intensity of preference.

items.label: Quadratic Voting
items.description: Members use credits to vote, with the cost increasing quadratically for multiple votes on the same option.

items.label: Continuous Voting
items.description: Members can change their votes over time, with decisions finalized when a threshold is reached.

items.label: Holacracy
items.description: Decision-making authority is distributed across self-organizing teams.

items.label: Collaborative Platforms
items.description: Structured discussions on tools like Loomio or Polis are used to make group decisions.

items.label: Deliberative Polling
items.description: Members discuss and reflect on an issue before voting, informed by deliberation.

items.label: Investor-Filled Board Seats
items.description: Key decisions are made by a board with seats allocated to investors or stakeholders.

items.label: Elected Board of Directors
items.description: Members elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf.

items.label: Advisory Committees
items.description: Smaller groups provide recommendations, which the broader organization typically follows.

items.label: Delegated Decision-Making
items.description: Specific individuals or groups are entrusted with decision-making authority.

items.label: Executive Committees
items.description: A subset of leaders or senior members makes critical decisions.

items.label: First Past the Post
items.description: The option with the most votes wins, regardless of whether it achieves a majority.

items.label: Lottery/Sortition
items.description: Members or leaders are randomly selected to make decisions, promoting fairness.

items.label: Proof of Work
items.description: Decision weight is tied to demonstrable effort or contributions, common in blockchain systems.

items.label: Random Choice
items.description: Decisions are made by chance, such as a coin toss or drawing lots, to avoid bias.

items.label: Algorithm-Driven Decisions
items.description: Automated systems analyze data and propose or enforce decisions.

items.label: Autocratic Decision-Making
items.description: A single leader or authority makes all decisions without group input.

items.label: Hierarchical Decision-Making
items.description: Decisions are made at different levels of an organizational structure, with authority increasing at higher levels.

items.label: Negotiated Decisions
items.description: Stakeholders or parties discuss and negotiate until they reach an agreement.
